label: John 9:1
text: As he passed by, he saw a man blind from birth.

label: John 9:2
text: His disciples asked him, “Rabbi, who sinned, this man or his parents, that he was born blind?”

label: John 9:3
text:
Jesus answered,
“Neither did this man sin, nor his parents; but, that the works of God might be revealed in him.

label: John 9:4
text: I must work the works of him who sent me, while it is day. The night is coming, when no one can work.

label: John 9:5
text: While I am in the world, I am the light of the world.”

label: John 9:6
text: When he had said this, he spat on the ground, made mud with the saliva, anointed the blind man’s eyes with the mud,

label: John 9:7
text:
and said to him,
“Go, wash in the pool of Siloam” (which means “Sent”). So he went away, washed, and came back seeing.

label: John 9:8
text: The neighbors therefore, and those who saw that he was blind before, said, “Isn’t this he who sat and begged?”

label: John 9:9
text:
Others were saying, “It is he.” Still others were saying, “He looks like him.”
He said, “I am he.”

label: John 9:10
text: They therefore were asking him, “How were your eyes opened?”

label: John 9:11
text:
He answered, “A man called Jesus made mud, anointed my eyes, and said to me,
‘Go to the pool of Siloam, and wash.’ So I went away and washed, and I received sight.”

label: John 9:12
text:
Then they asked him, “Where is he?”
He said, “I don’t know.”

label: John 9:13
text: They brought him who had been blind to the Pharisees.

label: John 9:14
text: It was a Sabbath when Jesus made the mud and opened his eyes.

label: John 9:15
text: Again therefore the Pharisees also asked him how he received his sight. He said to them, “He put mud on my eyes, I washed, and I see.”

label: John 9:16
text: Some therefore of the Pharisees said, “This man is not from God, because he doesn’t keep the Sabbath.” Others said, “How can a man who is a sinner do such signs?” There was division among them.

label: John 9:17
text:
Therefore they asked the blind man again, “What do you say about him, because he opened your eyes?”
He said, “He is a prophet.”

label: John 9:18
text: The Jews therefore did not believe concerning him, that he had been blind, and had received his sight, until they called the parents of him who had received his sight,

label: John 9:19
text: and asked them, “Is this your son, whom you say was born blind? How then does he now see?”

label: John 9:20
text: His parents answered them, “We know that this is our son, and that he was born blind;

label: John 9:21
text: but how he now sees, we don’t know; or who opened his eyes, we don’t know. He is of age. Ask him. He will speak for himself.”

label: John 9:22
text: His parents said these things because they feared the Jews; for the Jews had already agreed that if any man would confess him as Christ, he would be put out of the synagogue.

label: John 9:23
text: Therefore his parents said, “He is of age. Ask him.”

label: John 9:24
text: So they called the man who was blind a second time, and said to him, “Give glory to God. We know that this man is a sinner.”

label: John 9:25
text: He therefore answered, “I don’t know if he is a sinner. One thing I do know: that though I was blind, now I see.”

label: John 9:26
text: They said to him again, “What did he do to you? How did he open your eyes?”

label: John 9:27
text: He answered them, “I told you already, and you didn’t listen. Why do you want to hear it again? You don’t also want to become his disciples, do you?”

label: John 9:28
text: They insulted him and said, “You are his disciple, but we are disciples of Moses.

label: John 9:29
text: We know that God has spoken to Moses. But as for this man, we don’t know where he comes from.”

label: John 9:30
text: The man answered them, “How amazing! You don’t know where he comes from, yet he opened my eyes.

label: John 9:31
text: We know that God doesn’t listen to sinners, but if anyone is a worshiper of God, and does his will, he listens to him.

label: John 9:32
text: Since the world began it has never been heard of that anyone opened the eyes of someone born blind.

label: John 9:33
text: If this man were not from God, he could do nothing.”

label: John 9:34
text: They answered him, “You were altogether born in sins, and do you teach us?” They threw him out.

label: John 9:35
text:
Jesus heard that they had thrown him out, and finding him, he said,
“Do you believe in the Son of God?”

variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of John' lists εις τον υιον του ανθρωπου ('in the Son of Man') for Papyri 66 and 75, א (Sinaiticus), B (Vaticanus), D, W (Washingtonianus), 397, it d, syr s and co sa, against εις τον υιον του θεου ('in the Son of God'), the reading the WEB prints, for A, K, L, X, Δ, Θ, Ψ, Byz and others.

label: John 9:36
text: He answered, “Who is he, Lord, that I may believe in him?”

label: John 9:37
text:
Jesus said to him,
“You have both seen him, and it is he who speaks with you.”

label: John 9:38
text: He said, “Lord, I believe!” and he worshiped him.

label: John 9:39
text:
Jesus said,
“I came into this world for judgment, that those who don’t see may see; and that those who see may become blind.”

label: John 9:40
text: Those of the Pharisees who were with him heard these things, and said to him, “Are we also blind?”

label: John 9:41
text:
Jesus said to them,
“If you were blind, you would have no sin; but now you say, ‘We see.’ Therefore your sin remains.

label: A man blind from birth
statement: As he passed by, Jesus saw a man who had been blind from his birth.
note: The man is unnamed; later church tradition calls him Celidonius (recorded on the person node).

label: Congenital blindness read as punishment for sin
statement: The disciples asked whether the man's congenital blindness was punishment for his own sin or his parents' - affliction was assumed to trace to sin.
note: The question presupposes the common link between affliction and sin; Jesus rejects it in 9:3.

label: Jesus made clay and anointed the blind man's eyes
statement: Jesus spat on the ground, made clay with the saliva, and anointed the blind man's eyes with the clay.
note: Miracle narrative written neutrally and searched honestly; recorded as none-found, as in Matthew and Mark for comparable healings.

label: Saliva applied to afflicted eyes as a healing gesture
statement: Applying saliva to afflicted eyes was a recognized healing gesture in the first-century world.
note: The gesture, not the healing, is the checkable custom.

label: The man washed in Siloam and came back seeing
statement: The man went, washed in the pool of Siloam, and came back seeing.
note: Miracle claim written neutrally and searched honestly; recorded as none-found.

label: The pool of Siloam, whose name means 'Sent'
statement: The pool of Siloam, whose name means 'Sent', was a pool at southern Jerusalem to which people went to wash.
note: The wordplay on shalach (send) belongs to the narrative; the checkable fact is the pool and its name.

label: The blind man sat and begged
statement: The man was known to his neighbours as one who used to sit and beg - begging as the livelihood of the blind.
note: The neighbours' recognition presupposes his regular begging station.

label: Making clay on the Sabbath treated as forbidden labour
statement: It was a Sabbath when Jesus made the clay and opened the man's eyes; kneading (making clay) was among the labours forbidden on the Sabbath.
note: The narrative times the sign on a Sabbath so that the kneading of clay falls under Sabbath law.

label: The Pharisees divided over the Sabbath sign
statement: Some Pharisees said 'This man is not from God, because he doesn't keep the Sabbath'; others asked how a sinner could do such signs - they were divided.
note: A specific report of division; the wider Sabbath-healing dispute is attested separately (see related_to).

label: The leaders called the man's parents to verify his blindness
statement: The Jewish leaders did not believe he had been blind and received sight, so they called his parents, who confirmed he was born blind but refused to say how he now saw.
note: The parents' confirmation of congenital blindness (9:20-21) belongs to this claim.

label: An agreed rule: confessing Jesus as Christ meant expulsion from the synagogue
statement: The Jewish authorities had already agreed that anyone who confessed Jesus as the Christ would be put out of the synagogue (aposynagogos).
note: The parents' fear (9:21-23) presupposes this standing agreement; the Birkat ha-Minim debate is recorded at grade D.

label: 'We are disciples of Moses; God spoke to Moses'
statement: The leaders answered: 'We are disciples of Moses. We know that God has spoken to Moses' - the Torah of Moses as their final religious authority.
note: The appeal to Mosaic authority as the decisive norm in a legal dispute.

label: 'Never since the world began was it heard that anyone opened the eyes of one born blind'
statement: The healed man said it had never been heard that anyone opened the eyes of someone born blind.
note: The man's claim within the narrative; what can be checked is the surrounding expectation of messianic healing of the blind.

label: The leaders cast the man out
statement: The leaders answered 'You were altogether born in sins', and cast him out - the expulsion of 9:22 carried out on the man himself.
note: The Greek (exebalon auton) is read as expulsion from the synagogue community.

label: Jesus found the man; 'Do you believe in the Son of God?'; he worshiped him
statement: After his expulsion Jesus found the man and asked 'Do you believe in the Son of God?' (early witnesses: 'Son of Man'); the man confessed 'Lord, I believe' and worshiped him.
note: The Son of God / Son of Man reading difference is recorded as a variant on passage:jn-09-35.
